title: Nematoda Agricultural Pests 64-species x 16-locus design (PREPRINT-27 dimensions) vs. published phylum-wide phylogenomics
purpose: End-to-end seqnet -> RuNIE validation sweep at the dataset dimensions of PREPRINT-27 (nematoda-agricultural-pests-preprint): 64 species across 14 Nematoda families and 16 loci (14 mitochondrial loci + nuclear SSU_18S + LSU_28S). PREPRINT-27 only sets the taxon strata and quotas; it is not a validation source. Final trees are scored against deep phylum clades and infraordinal plant-parasitic groupings reported in the peer-reviewed studies below. A clade is testable when the run samples >= 2 tips inside and >= 2 outside it, and recovered when the unrooted tree contains the corresponding bipartition.

design_reference.taxon_design: 4 outgroups (2 Rhabditidae, 1 Cephalobidae, 1 Heterorhabditidae), 6 Clade I Dorylaimia virus-vector ectoparasites (4 Longidoridae, 2 Trichodoridae), 10 Panagrolaimomorpha & Aphelenchoidea (3 Steinernematidae, 7 Aphelenchoididae), 12 basal Tylenchomorpha ecto-/semi-endoparasites (3 Criconematidae, 3 Tylenchulidae, 3 Anguinidae, 3 Hoplolaimidae), 10 migratory endoparasites (10 Pratylenchidae), 11 cyst nematodes (11 Heteroderidae), and 11 root-knot nematodes (11 Meloidogynidae).
design_reference.taxonomy_note: Most Chromadorean nematodes (Rhabditida/Tylenchida/Aphelenchida) lack mitochondrial atp8, retaining 12 mitochondrial PCGs + 2 rRNAs. Families without abundant complete mitogenomes on NCBI (Criconematidae, Tylenchulidae, Anguinidae, Hoplolaimidae, Trichodoridae) are supplemented automatically by seqnet via per-locus mitochondrial COI/COII/CYTB/16S/12S queries alongside nuclear SSU 18S and LSU 28S rRNA.
design_reference.locus_interpretation: 14 mitochondrial loci (12 Chromadorean PCGs + 16S rrnL + 12S rrnS) + nuclear SSU_18S + LSU_28S = 16 orthologous phylogenomic loci. Horizontally transferred plant-cell-wall degrading enzymes (GH5/PL3/expansins), dorsal/subventral stylet effectors, stress chaperones, and nematicide target CYP450/receptor families are analyzed separately in Stage 4 codon-selection sweeps.

scored_clades.name: Clade I/II Enoplea-Dorylaimia (Longidoridae + Trichodoridae vs. Chromadorea)

support.statement: Deep split separates Enoplea (Dorylaimida/Triplonchida Clades 1-2) from Chromadorea (Clades 8-12)
Dorylaimia (including Longidoridae) + Enoplia recovered sister to Chromadorea with full phylogenomic support
Clade 12 Tylenchomorpha forms a strongly supported radiation uniting foliar, migratory, and sedentary plant parasites
Tylenchida families cluster within Clade 12 sister to Aphelenchoididae
Hoplolaimidae, Pratylenchidae, Heteroderidae, and Meloidogynidae form the crown plant-parasitic Subclade 12B
Sedentary root-knot and cyst nematodes share expanded HGT cellulase and pectate lyase arsenals inherited from a tylenchid ancestor
Longidoridae (Xiphinema + Longidorus) forms a monophyletic Clade 2 dorylaimid family
Longidoridae maximally supported as a cohesive Clade 2 plant-ectoparasitic lineage
Bursaphelenchus and Aphelenchoides form a distinct Clade 10B fungal/plant-parasitic radiation
Aphelenchoididae constitutes a cohesive Clade 10 lineage separated from Clade 12 Tylenchida
Heterodera + Globodera cyst nematodes form a strongly supported derived clade within Subclade 12B
Heteroderidae strongly supported with syncytium-inducing sedentary parasitism
Meloidogyne forms a maximally supported monophyletic root-knot clade inside Subclade 12B
Root-knot nematodes share a derived giant-cell endoparasitic genomic architecture

report_only_clades.name: Tylenchomorpha + Aphelenchoididae relationship
report_only_clades.why_not_scored: Aphelenchoidea was historically placed with Tylenchida, whereas Holterman2006, vanMegen2009, and Kikuchi2011 place Aphelenchoididae in Clade 10B with Panagrolaimomorpha/Steinernematidae rather than Clade 12.

report_only_clades.name: Pratylenchidae (monophyly check)
report_only_clades.why_not_scored: Pratylenchidae (Pratylenchus, Nacobbus, Hirschmanniella, Radopholus) is known to be paraphyletic with respect to Hoplolaimidae, Heteroderidae, and Meloidogynidae in Holterman2006 and vanMegen2009.
